Q1: At the keep_fixing round cap, what should happen to a `keep_fixing` decision on a high, critical or unrated finding (severity missing or not one of critical/high/medium/low)?
Choices:
A) Convert it to `fail`. The existing `failed_count > 0` branch then stops the project as `ai:security-pass-failed`. It can still recover through `/re-security-pass`, `/security-pass-waive`, or the automatic reset when the engine changes. Medium and low `keep_fixing` decisions are still converted to advisories as they are today. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Leave it as `keep_fixing`, which opens one more fix cycle. Add a new hard ceiling with a default, such as `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_BLOCKING_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS`, after which it becomes `fail`.
C) Leave it as `keep_fixing` with no new ceiling, bounded only by `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS`. **Note:** that setting defaults to `0` (unbounded), which brings back the endless fix-cycle loop seen in project #3965.
Q2: Should the fix also stop the judge itself from choosing `accept_with_followup` for high, critical or unrated findings in any round, not only at the cap?
Choices:
A) Yes. In the poller, rewrite any judge `accept_with_followup` on a high, critical or unrated finding: to `keep_fixing` while keep_fixing rounds remain, and to the Q1 outcome once they are spent. Also add a matching rule to the exhaustion-judge prompt. Human `/security-pass-waive` stays allowed. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Only change the cap conversion at line 6861, as the finding describes. The judge can still choose to waive high-severity findings itself.
